summary: getMatchesAfterId cursor pagination is broken: WHERE m.id > $1 combined with ORDER BY m.play_date DESC returns newest matches first, so the cursor (last match ID from previous page) never advances — frontend gets stuck on the same first page of matches.
failure_scenario: User scrolls to load more matches. First page returns matches with IDs 200-151 (newest). X-Next-Cursor = 151. Second call with after=151: WHERE m.id > 151 returns matches 200-152 again (same matches because newest are still > 151). Infinite loop returning the same matches.

summary: getVerificationKeyForVerify() now returns the DERIVEd public key (from RSA_PRIVATE_KEY) instead of the original public key string. For users who configured RSA_PUBLIC_KEY explicitly, the derived public key may differ (different key pair) or the old rsaPublicKey path was skipped — causing RS256 verification to silently fall back to HS256 when only RSA_PRIVATE_KEY is set and RSA_PUBLIC_KEY is missing.
failure_scenario: User has RSA_PRIVATE_KEY configured but no RSA_PUBLIC_KEY (common in single-file deployments). verifyToken() calls getVerificationKeyForVerify() which derives public key from private key — this works. But if both keys are set and differ (separate key pair for signing vs verification), the derived public key won't match the signing key, and RS256 verification fails for all tokens signed with the original private key.

summary: /metrics endpoint now uses getRealClientIP(req) instead of req.ip, adding unnecessary header parsing overhead on every Prometheus scrape (every 15-30s). getRealClientIP() reads 6+ HTTP headers; req.ip is a single property that already respects trust proxy.
failure_scenario: High-traffic production server with Prometheus scraping /metrics every 15s. Each scrape now parses X-Forwarded-For, CF-Connecting-IP, X-Real-IP, etc. from request headers, adding ~50-100 microseconds per scrape. Over a year, this is thousands of unnecessary header reads. Functionally correct but a resource regression for a high-frequency endpoint.

summary: switchTab made async with try/catch rollback, but the init-time call at line 344 (this.switchTab('rankings')) is NOT awaited. If rankings render throws, the UI has already switched to the rankings tab (nav highlight + tab content shown) and only THEN rolls back — creating a brief flash of incorrect UI state. Previously, a synchronous throw would propagate to the outer init() catch block and show an error message; now the error is swallowed inside switchTab, the UI flickers, and the user sees a transient error toast before the page recovers.
failure_scenario: User loads the app. Rankings API is down. Previously: init() catches the error, shows 'Hệ thống đã sẵn sàng' never appears, user sees error state. Now: switchTab switches UI to rankings tab (visible), renderRankings throws, catch block rolls back UI, shows toast 'Lỗi khi tải tab rankings'. User sees a brief flash of the rankings tab before it disappears.

summary: initRateLimitRedis changed from sync (no-op if client already exists) to async (waits up to 5s for Redis readiness). This adds 5 seconds to server startup when Redis is down, during which NO requests are served. The old behavior was: create the IORedis client at module load (line 23), and let the SCRIPT LOAD handler on line 53 handle the startup race by falling back to a dummy store. The new explicit await blocks startup.
failure_scenario: Redis is down during a deployment. Old behavior: server starts in ~2s, first few requests use dummy store (fail-open). New behavior: server blocks for 5s waiting for Redis, then starts with dummy store. During those 5s, users see connection timeouts instead of a slow server. This is a regression for deployments where Redis is temporarily unavailable.

summary: systemRouter capture change: const systemRouter = createSystemRouter(routeCtx) followed by app.use('/', systemRouter). The sseCleanupInterval is now attached as a property on the router object. The shutdown handler at line 571 (systemRouter?.sseCleanupInterval) correctly accesses this. However, if createSystemRouter is ever called multiple times (e.g., hot-reload in dev), each call creates a new sseCleanupInterval that is never cleared, causing a memory leak of stale cleanup intervals.
failure_scenario: Developer runs npm run dev-full, makes a code change to system.js, Vite hot-reloads server.js. createSystemRouter is called again, creating a new sseCleanupInterval. The old interval (5-min periodic IP cleanup) is never cleared. After 20 hot-reloads, there are 20 stale intervals each deleting from ipConnections every 5 minutes — minor but growing.
